verdict.label: STEP ASIDE — Reconstitution Bid Failed; Five-Session Nasdaq Bleed; NFP Binary July 2
verdict.rationale_short: The morning's STEP ASIDE call was correct on direction — SPX closed at 7,354.02 (-0.05%), its fifth consecutive session below 7,460 — but wrong on the two headline narratives. First, NVDA fell 1.64% to $192.53 despite being the #1 Russell 3000 constituent and the primary target of the record $334B closing cross; the passive Growth ETF bid was overwhelmed by active tech selling, confirming institutional distribution rather than accumulation. Second, the Hormuz oil panic reversed entirely: Brent crude settled at $71.99 (-4.34%), below even the June 25 close of ~$72.50, as more tankers exited the Strait and Trump labeled the drone strike a 'foolish violation of our Ceasefire Agreement.' The inflation risk headlined in the morning brief did not materialize. The net regime: five of six indicators remain breached (VIX 18.89, DXY 101.25, SPX below 7,460, BTC at new intraday low $58,189); the oil reversal preserves the disinflation narrative but does not clear any gate. The week's dominant event is the June Non-Farm Payrolls report, pulled forward to Thursday July 2 (markets closed July 3), with consensus at +172K and any strong read cementing BofA's three-hike framework into a 3-day holiday weekend gap.

trade_setups.asset: IWM long / QQQ short — small-cap vs. mega-cap pair
trade_setups.thesis: Russell 2000 gained +0.71% on June 26 while Nasdaq fell -0.24% — the reconstitution created a structural small-cap bid that outperformed mega-cap Growth despite all three Growth ETF reconstitution beneficiaries (NVDA, MU, AMD) falling. Quarter-end window dressing (June 29-30) institutionally supports large-cap defensive and small-cap exposure over concentrated Nasdaq. The pair removes broad market beta and captures the regime-driven rotation from AI mega-cap toward value/small-cap that has been unfolding since June 23.

bear_case: The reconstitution's failure is the session's most important signal, and the market is not fully pricing what it implies. If $334B in passive Growth ETF buying — the largest liquidity event in Nasdaq closing-cross history — cannot produce a net positive close in NVDA, MU, or AMD, then the active selling overhang in mega-cap tech is larger than the passive buying program. Quarter-end window dressing (June 29-30) provides a smaller and more discretionary bid that faces the same headwind. Five consecutive Nasdaq losing sessions and a weekly SPX decline of 1.73% establish a pattern: every attempted recovery has been sold. The NFP on July 2 — with markets closed July 3 — is particularly dangerous: a strong employment print (+200K, wages +0.4%) arrives into a 3-day weekend gap with no ability to rebalance. SPX reopening July 7 with the full weight of a near-certain September hike, an intact OpenAI IPO delay, and a Nasdaq that failed to hold five consecutive recovery attempts would establish 7,300 as resistance rather than support. If SPX closes below 7,300 at any point before July 7, the STEP ASIDE framework escalates to BEARISH and the BofA hike-cycle framework extends into a full-year headwind for growth multiples. Invalidation: SPX closes above 7,460 AND VIX closes below 17 simultaneously — STEP ASIDE reverts to HOLD. NFP prints 130-180K with wages +0.2-0.3% (Goldilocks) — regime conditions stabilize.
